definition: A strong, lasting liking for something or a habit of doing it.
example: My grandfather has a penchant for telling long stories at the dinner table.
nuance: A penchant is a settled taste, often a quirky one, while a whim is a passing impulse that fades quickly.
prompt: A college student describes her roommate's habits to a friend.
options: My roommate has a penchant for rearranging our furniture every few weeks.
My roommate wears a silver penchant on a thin chain around her neck.
My roommate has a penchant for loud music, so she avoids it whenever she can.
My roommate showed a penchant for baking once last Tuesday and never again.
reasons: A habit she keeps coming back to shows a lasting taste for doing it.
This confuses the word with pendant, a piece of jewelry that hangs from a chain.
Avoiding something is the opposite of having a fondness for it.
Something done once is not a lasting tendency or a settled taste.

practice.prompt: A teacher writes end-of-year comments about several students.
options: Lena has a real penchant for math, which is why she dreads every algebra quiz.
Ava penchant her essay neatly in blue ink before handing it in.
Jordan has a penchant for catching colds and hates missing class because of them.
Marcus has a penchant for asking questions that push our discussions deeper.
reasons: Dreading a subject contradicts having a strong taste for it.
The word is a noun naming a liking; it is not a verb meaning to write.
Getting sick is unwanted and involuntary, not a taste or a chosen habit.
A repeated habit he clearly enjoys fits the idea of an enduring liking.
